root_cause.text: KVM x86 MMU applied a PFN-change WARN sanity check to shadow MMUs even though shadow-present SPTEs can legitimately become stale when host/userspace modifies shadowed guest PTEs outside KVM’s write tracking, causing false warning-triggered fault handling.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `else if (WARN_ON_ONCE(pfn != spte_to_pfn(*sptep)))` to first test `pfn != spte_to_pfn(*sptep)` and only `WARN_ON_ONCE(vcpu->arch.mmu->root_role.direct)`, while the commit message states that in MMUs with shadowed gPTEs, “writes from outside the scope of KVM, e.g. from host userspace, aren't detected by KVM's write tracking and so can break KVM's shadow paging rules.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Always invalidate mismatched SPTEs but only warn when a PFN mismatch occurs in direct MMU mode.
intent_record.what: The condition `else if (WARN_ON_ONCE(pfn != spte_to_pfn(*sptep)))` was changed to `else if (pfn != spte_to_pfn(*sptep))`, and a new statement `WARN_ON_ONCE(vcpu->arch.mmu->root_role.direct);` was inserted inside that branch before calling `drop_spte(vcpu->kvm, sptep)` and setting `flush = true`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now always handles a PFN mismatch by dropping the SPTE and requesting a flush, while the warning is narrowed to trigger only when the MMU is in direct mode. This preserves the mismatch recovery behavior but avoids warning on every mismatch case, warning only for the mode where such a mismatch is considered unexpected.

grouping_result.intent: Always invalidate mismatched SPTEs but only warn when a PFN mismatch occurs in direct MMU mode.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it removes the PFN-mismatch warning behavior for shadow MMUs while still invalidating stale SPTEs, and limits WARNs to direct MMU mode where the sanity check is valid.

candidates.rationale: This statement is the direct root cause: it unconditionally triggers a WARN on PFN mismatch for shadow-present SPTEs, even though such mismatches are legitimate in shadow MMU mode when guest PTEs are modified outside KVM write tracking.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition unconditionally emits a WARN when the PFN differs from the PFN encoded in a shadow-present SPTE. In shadow MMU mode, such PFN changes can legitimately occur when host/userspace modifies shadowed guest PTEs outside KVM write tracking, so applying this WARN sanity check here causes false warning-triggered fault handling.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the exact logic in `mmu_set_spte()` that the root cause discusses. The vulnerable construct is present in this commit: inside `if (is_shadow_present_pte(*sptep))`, the code now warns on PFN change for a shadow-present SPTE via `} else if (WARN_ON_ONCE(pfn != spte_to_pfn(*sptep))) {`. This matches the stated root cause: applying a PFN-change WARN sanity check to shadow MMUs even though shadow-present SPTEs can legitimately become stale. The prefetch path was also changed from `if (prefetch && is_last_spte(*sptep, level)) return RET_PF_SPURIOUS;` to only treat it as spurious when `pfn == spte_to_pfn(*sptep)`, i.e. `if (prefetch && is_last_spte(*sptep, level) && pfn == spte_to_pfn(*sptep)) return RET_PF_SPURIOUS;`, so PFN-changed cases now fall through to the warning path. Because this commit introduces the WARN on PFN changes rather than removing or restricting it for shadow MMU cases, the fix for the described vulnerability is not present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the exact SPTE replacement logic and the PFN-change handling. The vulnerable construct is present in the branch `else if (pfn != spte_to_pfn(*sptep))` at lines 2036-2040. When an existing rmap SPTE maps a different PFN than the new one, the code logs `"hfn old %llx new %llx\n"`, then unconditionally executes `drop_spte(vcpu->kvm, sptep);` and `kvm_flush_remote_tlbs(vcpu->kvm);`. Per the root cause, shadow-present SPTEs can legitimately become stale when host/userspace modifies shadowed guest PTEs outside KVM write tracking, so treating PFN mismatch here as a sanity-check failure is the vulnerable behavior. The fix would be to avoid applying this PFN-change sanity handling to shadow MMUs / shadow-present SPTEs, but no such distinction or guard exists in this function. Instead, PFN mismatch is handled generically for any rmap SPTE. Therefore the buggy construct is present and the fix is not yet in this code.
